# ETSI TS 119 612 v2.4.1 live-v6 conformance evidence

`manifest.tsv` records the exact 31 UTF-8 national trusted-list documents selected from the authenticated Commission LOTL on 2026-09-17. Each row fixes the source document by SHA-256; all 31 documents pass portable projection. The documents themselves are not copied into the repository because they are signed, mutable publications owned by their scheme operators.

The stable derived cases in `tests/tsl_parse/etsi_119612_v2_4_1_tests.rs` reproduce the parser semantics exercised by those documents without copying operator data. The manifest's final column identifies the corresponding test.

## Clause decisions

- Clauses 5.1.4, 5.3.5.2, and 5.4.3.2 are applied by semantic URI role. Language tags are bounded lower-case RFC 5646 tags. Contact values must satisfy their URI role, with a narrow compatibility normalization for a host-shaped provider information value that omitted `https://`; no position-based role inference is used.
- Clause 5.3.11 permits multilingual legal-notice text. Annex E.2 prohibits TAB, CR, and LF, but the signed Commission LOTL and selected national publications contain layout line breaks in `TSLLegalNotice`. The legal-notice parser alone maps those layout characters to spaces before applying the ordinary bounded-text policy. Names, identifiers, and all other multilingual fields continue to reject prohibited controls.
- Clause 5.4.2 requires an official provider identifier in `TSPTradeName`. The projection retains every authenticated VAT/NTR value, accepts deployed spacing variants, and can recover the same organization identifier from a service certificate. Where a legacy publication provides no such value, a scheme-scoped internal NTR key is derived for grouping only and is never represented as an official registry assertion.
- Clause 5.5.3 defines a PKI service identity by its public key. Multiple certificates are accepted only after proving identical SubjectPublicKeyInfo; exact duplicate certificates and repeated service rows are coalesced. A structured `Other` alongside an independently valid certificate contributes no identity claim. A service without PKI can retain a bounded opaque scheme identifier, as deployed lists do, without interpreting it as a network location.
- Clauses 5.5.5 and 5.6.3 are applied together after signature authentication. A pre-published future current state is replaced by the newest historical state effective at trusted evaluation time only when both states bind the same SKI; a not-yet-effective service is omitted. Historical certificates are verified against the historical SKI and then discarded, while history that cannot identify a key is omitted rather than used for a trust decision.
- Clause 5.5.9.2.2.2 requires certificate-policy Object Identifiers. XAdES `OIDAsURN`, `OIDAsURI`, and the deployed single-trailing-dot form are normalized to canonical dotted decimal. A malformed noncritical qualification contributes no claim; malformed critical qualification semantics fail closed.
- Clause 5.5.9.3 `TakenOverBy` is parsed with its scheme-specific `OtherQualifier` subtree bounded but uninterpreted, as the clause does not assign validation behavior to that qualifier. Unknown critical extension semantics still fail closed; Annex B permits unknown noncritical extension subtrees to be ignored.
- X.509 ingestion retains bounded legacy serial encodings and noncritical extensions needed to publish authenticated historical anchors. Unknown or unprojectable public-key properties remain typed as `Other`, so algorithm allow-lists and strength policy continue to reject them during chain evaluation rather than guessing security properties.

The normative reference is [ETSI TS 119 612 V2.4.1 (2025-08)](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_TS/119600_119699/119612/02.04.01_60/ts_119612v020401p.pdf). This evidence covers typed projection; native ingestion authenticates the Commission LOTL and national-list XML signatures before applying evaluation-time state selection.
